answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay, and within 15 minutes at 1-800-746-1553 once it knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once it knows or should know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: This applies to an accident involving a death of an individual at the mine.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must have an incombustible content of not less than 80 percent where no methane is present. The 80 percent minimum rises only when methane is present in a ventilating current.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The percentage is increased only where methane is present in a ventilating current.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: The operator must make available to each underground miner an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. Each drill must be held for each shift at a time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

claims.text: The drills must be held for each shift at a time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. Approximately 8 of those hours are given at the minesite.

claims.text: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Approximately 8 of those hours are given at the minesite.
claims.quote: approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, which is equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. This appears in both 30 CFR 56.9300 and 57.9300. Part 56 covers surface metal and nonmetal mines, and Part 57 covers underground metal and nonmetal mines. Berms may have openings as needed for roadway drainage.

claims.text: The same height requirement appears in section 57.9300.

claims.text: Berms may have openings to the extent necessary for roadway drainage.
claims.quote: Berms may have openings to the extent necessary for roadway drainage.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours. (A 48-hour option exists only if advance arrangements are made for additional supplies.)

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plans. They cover only MSHA respiratory protection and airborne contaminant rules.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The chunks don't say. They cover MSHA mining rules on slopes, shafts, buckets and ventilation controls. None of them covers OSHA construction trench requirements or the depth at which a protective system is needed.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site. They cover MSHA training, training records, and certified persons in mines.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The chunks do not say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover impoundment design plan requirements and permits for mining under bodies of water, not EPA stormwater permits.
